title: Network Fundamentals
summary: Move from network diagrams to interfaces, packets, bandwidth, and latency.
objectives: Explain the roles of a network interface, packet, bandwidth, and latency.
Interpret a simple network path without accessing a live external network.

vocab.def: The hardware or software point where a device connects to a network.
A small unit of data sent across a network.
The time it takes information to travel between points.
The amount of information a connection can carry over time.

sections.heading: Networks move packets
sections.body: Applications send information that is organized into packets. Network interfaces, switches, gateways, and links help packets travel from one system to another.

sections.heading: Speed has more than one meaning
sections.body: Bandwidth describes how much information a connection can carry. Latency describes travel time. A connection can have high bandwidth and still have noticeable latency.

sections.heading: Use a closed map
sections.body: Study a synthetic network map and trace a packet path. Do not scan, probe, or connect to external networks. Network learning stays inside approved diagrams or sandboxes.

practice.prompt: A video path has high bandwidth but high latency. What might a learner observe, and what does that observation not prove?

quiz.question: What does latency describe?
options: Time for information to travel between points
The amount of storage in a server
quiz.answer: Time for information to travel between points

lab.objective: Trace packets across a synthetic network map and compare bandwidth with latency.

reflectionPrompt: Which network measure would you want to inspect when a service feels slow, and why?
